title: Modern Data Engineering
tagline: From raw sources to a tested, governed lakehouse: the bridge from a CS degree to the work a data team does every day.
audience: Fresh CS graduates, or anyone comfortable with Python and basic SQL (SELECT, JOIN, GROUP BY). No data engineering experience needed.
prerequisites: Google Colab, or a laptop with uv. No Docker or cloud account. Lab 1.1 starts with 00_setup_check; see labs/README.md.

outcomes.text: Explain how a data platform fits together and choose between warehouse, lake and lakehouse
Write analytical SQL, including window functions, over databases and files
Build ingestion that is incremental and safe to re-run, from APIs and change feeds
Clean data, model it as a star schema and transform it with dbt under tests
Orchestrate pipelines and catch bad data before it reaches a report
Decide when Iceberg, Spark or streaming is worth it, and protect personal data under PDPL

case_study.name: Qafila

capstone.summary: Teams of 2–3 build a working data platform, choosing one of: Qafila Lakehouse: from raw sources to governed marts and an operations view; Open Data Platform: Saudi open datasets with tests and a small dashboard; Real-time Operations Monitor: replayed courier events, event-time KPIs and SLA alerts.
capstone.submission: Submit a public GitHub repository link before Day 5 with working code, a README, the grain of every fact table, and test results. Starter kit: labs/capstone/.
